'''''Limonium''''' is a genus of about 600 flowering plant species. Members are also known as '''sea-lavender''', '''statice''', '''caspia''' or '''marsh-rosemary'''. Despite their common names, species are not related to the [[lavender]]s or to [[rosemary]]. They are instead in [[Plumbaginaceae]], the plumbago or leadwort family.
The generic name is from the Latin ''{{lang|la|līmōnion}}'', used by [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]] for a wild plant and is ultimately derived from the Ancient Greek ''{{Transliteration|grc|leimon}}'' ({{lang|grc|[[wikt:λειμών|λειμών]]}}, 'meadow').<ref>{{OED|limonium}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The genus has a [[cosmopolitan distribution|subcosmopolitan]] distribution in Europe, Asia, Africa, North America and Australia. By far the greatest diversity (over 100 species) is in the area stretching from the [[Canary Islands]] east through the [[Mediterranean]] region to central Asia; for comparison, North America only has three native ''Limonium'' species.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=118606 Flora of North America]</ref>

==Description==
Sea-lavenders normally grow as [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]]s, growing 10–70 cm tall from a [[rhizome]]; a few (mainly from the Canary Islands) are woody [[shrub]]s up to 2 metres tall. Many species flourish in [[soil salinity|saline]] soils, and are therefore common near [[coast]]s and in [[salt marsh]]es, and also on saline, [[gypsum]] and [[alkaline]] soils in continental interiors.

The [[leaf|leaves]] are simple, entire to lobed, and from 1–30 cm long and 0.5–10 cm broad; most of the leaves are produced in a dense basal [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]], with the flowering stems bearing only small brown scale-leaves ([[bract]]s). The [[flower]]s are produced on a branched [[panicle]] or [[corymb]], the individual flowers are small (4–10 mm long) with a five-lobed [[calyx (flower)|calyx]] and [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]], and five [[stamen]]s; the flower colour is pink or violet to purple in most species, white or yellow in a few. Many of the species are [[apomixis|apomictic]]. The fruit is a small [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] containing a single [[seed]], partly enclosed by the persistent calyx.

==Features==
Several species are popular [[gardening|garden]] flowers; they are generally known to gardeners as ''statices''. They are grown both for their flowers and for the appearance of the [[Calyx (flower)|calyx]], which remains on the plant after the true flowers have fallen, and are known as "everlasting flowers".
